results.summary: The claim that op_ack_o is declared but never driven in keymgr_op_state_ctrl is false. op_ack_o is driven combinationally in every path of the always_comb block.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. In /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_op_state_ctrl.sv, op_ack_o has a default assignment of 1'b0 at line 53 (inside the always_comb at lines 50-107) and is explicitly set to 1'b1 in StAdv completion (line 76), StWait completion (line 94), and the default/error state (line 102). It is therefore fully driven and can never be X.
results.reasoning: keymgr_op_state_ctrl.sv lines 50-107 form a single always_comb that initializes op_ack_o=1'b0 (line 53) before the unique case. op_ack_o is then conditionally raised in StAdv (line 76: kmac_done_i && cnt==CDIs-1), StWait (line 94: kmac_done_i), and default (line 102). The downstream consumer keymgr_ctrl.sv connects op_ack at the .op_ack_o(op_ack) port (line 765) and uses it for sw_binding_unlock_o (line 202), op_done_o (line 448), and adv_state (line 459) — all of which work correctly because op_ack is fully driven. The evidence excerpt 'declared but not driven in this chunk' is an artifact of the LLM only seeing the port declarations, not the always_comb body. No defect.
results.formal_alignment: MISLEADING. formal_result.verdict=FAIL on '!$isunknown(op_ack_o)'. This contradicts the RTL: op_ack_o cannot be unknown because it has a combinational default. The FAIL is a spurious result of binding the property without the module body / proper environment.

results.summary: edn_done is a standard internal handshake term (edn_req & edn_ack), not a glitch-prone async signal. The 'must be $stable' property is semantically wrong for a handshake.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv line 43: assign edn_done = edn_req & edn_ack. edn_req is a registered flop (lines 48-57, clk_i domain) and edn_ack is the ack output of prim_edn_req (line 70), also in clk_i domain. A combinational AND of two clk_i-synchronous signals is normal RTL and is sampled cleanly by the clk_i flops that consume it (edn_req flop line 51, cnt_en flop line 88, prim_count clr_i line 100).
results.reasoning: edn_done feeds only clk_i-synchronous logic: it clears edn_req (line 51), sets cnt_en (line 88), and clears the reseed counter (line 100). All are evaluated on posedge clk_i, so any combinational settling is resolved before the next edge — there is no metastability or spurious sampling. Requiring edn_done to be $stable every cycle (the channel-B SVA) is incorrect: a handshake-done signal is expected to toggle. No defect.
results.formal_alignment: MISLEADING. formal FAIL on '$stable(edn_done)' simply reflects that a handshake signal toggles, which is correct behavior, not a bug.

results.summary: The assumption that edn_done is an externally controlled pulse is incorrect. It is an internal handshake signal, which is the intended design.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. In /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv, edn_done (line 43) is internally generated as edn_req & edn_ack and correctly used to terminate the request (edn_req cleared at lines 51-52) and to drive reseed_done_o (line 61). There is no external driver of edn_done in the design, and none is intended. The 'contradiction' is between two incorrect LLM assumptions, not between RTL and spec.
results.reasoning: The handshake works as: edn_req asserted (lines 53-55) -> prim_edn_req drives EDN bus and eventually returns edn_ack (line 70) -> edn_done = edn_req & edn_ack (line 43) -> edn_req cleared (lines 51-52), reseed_done_o pulsed (line 61), counter cleared (line 100). This is the standard OpenTitan EDN request pattern. No defect.

results.summary: init_i sampling in keymgr_cfg_en (gated by en_i) and the StSideloadReset-only use of init_i in keymgr_sideload_key_ctrl are both intended one-way initialization semantics. No defect, and the finding conflates two different modules.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. In /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_cfg_en.sv lines 40-48, init_q is set only when (init_i && en_i) and cleared on (init_q && !en_i); there is no state machine, so 'StSideloadReset' does not apply to this module. In /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_sideload_key_ctrl.sv lines 96-101, init_i is examined only in StSideloadReset to move to StSideloadIdle, which is the intended one-shot initialization. Ignoring init_i afterward is by design.
results.reasoning: The SVA binds 'state_q != StSideloadReset' to keymgr_ctrl, but keymgr_ctrl has no StSideloadReset state (its states are StCtrl*; see keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 110-122) — StSideloadReset lives in keymgr_sideload_key_ctrl (line 55). The property is mis-bound (status NAME_UNVERIFIED). In keymgr_cfg_en, init_i latching once en_i is high is the documented behavior for a 'has been initialized' indicator. The cfg_regwen instance uses init_i(1'b1) (keymgr.sv line 342) and the sw_binding_regwen instance uses init_i(init) (keymgr.sv line 365); both rely on the latch-and-hold semantics intentionally. No defect on the init_q / state_d path.
results.formal_alignment: INCONCLUSIVE. The property references StSideloadReset against the wrong module (keymgr_ctrl), status NAME_UNVERIFIED; it does not establish a real defect.

results.summary: valid_tracking_q is fully driven and used. The claim that it is declared but unconnected is false.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. In /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_sideload_key_ctrl.sv, valid_tracking_q is declared at line 190 and driven by a per-slot generate-for with an always_ff at lines 191-201: async clear on !rst_ni (line 194), sync clear on slot_clr[i] (line 195-196), and set on slot_sel[i] (line 197-198), retaining value otherwise. It is consumed at line 214 to compute sideload_sel_err_o = |(~valid_tracking_q & valids).
results.reasoning: The exact reset/clear/hold behavior the finding claims is 'missing' is precisely what lines 191-201 implement, matching the three guarantee excerpts. The signal is the SIDE_LOAD_SEL.CTRL.CONSISTENCY security countermeasure (comment line 203). The evidence excerpt that calls it 'declared but not assigned or used in this continuous region' is wrong — it is assigned in a sequential generate block, not a continuous region. No defect.
results.formal_alignment: MISLEADING. formal FAIL on the $stable property is spurious; the RTL implements exactly the stable/clear behavior the property describes.

results.summary: The finding confuses the prim_lfsr's optional entropy_i port (intentionally tied to 0) with the entropy supplied to keymgr_sideload_key_ctrl (real LFSR output). Sideload entropy is not zero.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. In /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv line 228, prim_lfsr is instantiated with .entropy_i('0). This is the LFSR's optional continuous entropy-mixing input, which is deliberately unused because the LFSR is reseeded from EDN via seed_en_i/seed_i (lines 226-227, fed by keymgr_reseed_ctrl seed_en_o/seed_o). The entropy consumed by keymgr_sideload_key_ctrl is data_rand (keymgr.sv line 594 .entropy_i(data_rand)), and data_rand[0]=lfsr[31:0], data_rand[1]=perm_data(lfsr[63:32]) (lines 240-241) — i.e., live LFSR output, not zero.
results.reasoning: The LFSR entropy chain: keymgr_reseed_ctrl fetches EDN entropy and drives seed_o/seed_en_o (keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv lines 31, 59, 71); these seed prim_lfsr (keymgr.sv lines 226-227). The LFSR is also advanced (lfsr_en) during operations. Its output lfsr[63:0] (line 229) is split into ctrl_rand and data_rand (lines 234-241). The prim_lfsr.entropy_i('0) port is a standard OpenTitan pattern when reseeding (not per-cycle entropy injection) is the entropy source. There is no security regression. No defect.
results.formal_alignment: MISLEADING. formal FAIL on '$changed(entropy_i)' targets the prim_lfsr entropy_i port which is correctly constant-0; this is intended and not the entropy that feeds key/sideload generation.

results.summary: The literal claim about RndCnstCdi entropy is a non-issue (cdi_sel is 1 bit, so the RndCnstCdi branch is unreachable and RndCnstCdi is a fixed netlist constant by design). However, inspecting the same key-output path (cdi_sel_o indexing key_state_q) reveals a real injected defect: in StCtrlInvalid the key output bypasses entropy randomization and drives the stored key state onto key_o.key.
results.root_cause: CONFIRMED (adjacent defect). /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 288-298 (always_comb key_output_ctrl). Upstream drives key_o.key[i] = invalid_stage_sel_o ? {EntropyRounds{entropy_i[i]}} : key_state_q[cdi_sel_o][i]. The modified RTL adds a carve-out (lines 289-297): 'if (invalid_stage_sel_o && (state_q == StCtrlInvalid)) key_o.key[i] = key_state_q[cdi_sel_o][i];' i.e. when in StCtrlInvalid with an invalid stage selection, the per-cycle entropy XOR/replacement is skipped and the raw stored key_state_q[cdi_sel_o] is placed on the key output bus. The source even carries the comment 'Subtle bug: During invalid states, expose unmasked key material by skipping the entropy XOR'. The literal F-0230 concern (sw_binding=RndCnstCdi when cdi_sel not 0/1) is a FALSE_ALARM: cdi_sel is CdiWidth=vbits(2)=1 bit (keymgr_pkg.sv lines 11-12), so cdi_sel can only be 0 or 1 and the RndCnstCdi fallback (keymgr.sv line 403) is dead code; RndCnstCdi is also a fixed design constant, never intended as runtime entropy.
results.trigger_condition: state_q == StCtrlInvalid AND invalid_stage_sel_o (stage_sel_o not in {Creator,OwnerInt,Owner}; in StCtrlInvalid stage_sel_o defaults to Disable, so invalid_stage_sel_o=1). In that state, key_o.key carries key_state_q[cdi_sel_o] instead of the fresh LFSR entropy that the correct design places on the bus.
results.security_impact: Defense-in-depth regression on the key output bus. The upstream design guarantees that whenever the stage selection is invalid, only fresh per-cycle entropy ever appears on key_o.key, so no stored key-state value is ever exposed in invalid/error states. The injected carve-out instead routes the stored key_state_q register onto the bus during StCtrlInvalid. Practical exposure is mitigated because StCtrlInvalid is reached via StCtrlWipe (keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 642-659) which wipes key_state with entropy (KeyUpdateWipe, lines 407-414), and because key_o.valid=op_req=0 in StCtrlInvalid (downstream sideload selects the sideload key when key_i.valid=0, keymgr_sideload_key_ctrl.sv line 217). Nonetheless it removes the intended re-randomization (the exposed value becomes static rather than per-cycle random) and makes the output's safety depend on the wipe having fully completed, weakening the secret-exposure countermeasure.
results.reasoning: Confirmed by comparison against upstream lowRISC keymgr_ctrl.sv, where the key output is a continuous assign / generate-for (gen_key_out_assign): 'assign key_o.key[i] = invalid_stage_sel_o ? {EntropyRounds{entropy_i[i]}} : key_state_q[cdi_sel_o][i];' with no StCtrlInvalid special case. The local file replaces this with a procedural always_comb (key_output_ctrl) that adds the StCtrlInvalid branch exposing key_state_q (lines 289-297) and self-documents it as a 'Subtle bug'. F-0230's involved spec keymgr_ctrl__always_comb__key_output_ctrl__001 and evidence excerpt '(1) if invalid_stage_sel_o and state_q == StCtrlInvalid, then key_state_q[cdi_sel_o][i] (unmasked)' point directly at this defect on the cdi_sel_o key-output path, so is_extra_finding=true. The original RndCnstCdi/cdi_sel concern is unfounded.
additional_findings: key_o.valid=0 in StCtrlInvalid (op_req not set, keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 676-679) limits direct downstream consumption.
cdi_sel_o is 1 bit, so cdi_sel_o is always a legal index 0/1; the RndCnstCdi fallback branch in keymgr.sv line 403 is unreachable.
results.formal_alignment: N/A for the literal claim (formalizability=none). The confirmed defect was found by direct RTL/upstream comparison, not by the (absent) formal property.

results.summary: Using creator_seed as the OwnerInt advance data while gating with owner_seed_vld is the intended OpenTitan design, confirmed identical to upstream.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv lines 462-463: assign adv_matrix[OwnerInt] = AdvDataWidth'({sw_binding, creator_seed}); assign adv_dvalid[OwnerInt] = owner_seed_vld. This matches the current upstream lowRISC master verbatim. The advance INTO OwnerInt (executed from the CreatorRootKey stage) deliberately mixes the creator seed, but the operation is gated on owner_seed validity because the owner seed must be present to proceed to the owner-intermediate stage.
results.reasoning: Verified against upstream (raw.githubusercontent.com/lowRISC/opentitan/master/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv): the OwnerInt data/valid pairing is exactly as in this file. adv_dvalid for the don't-care fill range [KeyMgrStages, 2**StageWidth-1] is tied to 1'b1 (line 408), but OwnerInt is a defined stage (keymgr_pkg.sv line 92, value 1) within KeyMgrStages=3, so it is NOT in the fill range — the guarantee-3 concern does not apply. The data/valid 'mismatch' is intended design semantics, not a wiring error. No defect.

results.summary: This is a vacuous high-level statement that correctness depends on submodule implementations; it asserts no checkable contradiction and the referenced submodules are correctly instantiated and checked.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. The 'assumption' (keymgr that input validation, KMAC control, and sideload handling depend on keymgr_input_checks / keymgr_kmac_if / keymgr_sideload_key_ctrl) is true and trivially satisfied: these are instantiated in /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv at u_checks (line 511), u_kmac_if (line 560), and u_sideload_ctrl (line 590), with FSM error checks wired to alerts (SideloadCtrlFsmCheck_A line 803). No specific input/state contradiction is asserted, so there is nothing to refute.
results.reasoning: The three submodules are connected and their outputs (valids, kmac_data_o.valid, sideload key validity) are consumed and cross-checked (sideload_sel_err, fsm_err) as the guarantee excerpts describe. The statement is a design-dependency observation, not a defect or contradiction. No issue in RTL.

results.summary: Gating the debug.invalid_* status flags to the relevant operation window is the intended behavior of these debug status registers, not a coverage gap.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv lines 542-548 gate each debug.invalid_*.de with the operation enable plus the relevant stage (e.g. invalid_creator_seed.de = adv_en & (stage_sel == Creator) & ~creator_seed_vld). These are software-readable debug hints that capture the cause of an operation failure during the operation that produced it; capturing them only in their meaningful window is by design. invalid_stage_sel_o (keymgr_ctrl.sv line 285) independently flags illegal stage selections.
results.reasoning: Invalid conditions outside an operation window are not silently lost in any security-relevant sense: actual faults are caught by keymgr_err (sync/async fault collection, keymgr_err.sv) and drive alerts, independent of the debug.invalid_* hints. The debug flags exist to explain why a given operation failed. This is intended design. Note: the unrelated key_output_ctrl block referenced by the same spec id (keymgr_ctrl__always_comb__key_output_ctrl__001) does contain a defect, but that is reported under F-0230; it is not what F-0233 alleges.
additional_findings: The injected unmasked-key-exposure defect in key_output_ctrl (keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 289-297) is reported under F-0230, not here.

results.summary: kmac_en_masking_i being used only in an elaboration-time assertion is an intentional, documented anti-tamper design choice, not a defect.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv lines 53-57 document that kmac_en_masking_i deliberately drives no functional logic (only ASSERT_INIT_NET KmacMaskCheck_A at line 786, plus unused_kmac_en_masking at lines 783-784) precisely so that, if boundary optimization were disabled, it would not present an obvious attack point. KmacEnMasking is a compile-time parameter (line 18) that actually controls masking behavior.
results.reasoning: The finding itself concludes it is 'more likely a verification-flow gap than a hardware defect.' The elaboration assertion KmacMaskCheck_A enforces KmacEnMasking == kmac_en_masking_i at build time; masking is functionally governed by the KmacEnMasking parameter (used in keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 209, 384-391, and keymgr_input_checks.sv line 83). Removal of assertions at synthesis does not change functional behavior. Intended design. No defect.

results.summary: Deriving ctrl_rand and data_rand from opposite LFSR halves with one half permuted is a deliberate decorrelation measure, matching upstream.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv lines 237-241: ctrl_rand[0]=lfsr[63:32], ctrl_rand[1]=perm_data(lfsr[31:0]); data_rand[0]=lfsr[31:0], data_rand[1]=perm_data(lfsr[63:32]). The asymmetry (swapped halves + permutation on share 1) is intentional so the control and data consumers receive decorrelated randomness from the same LFSR. perm_data is defined in keymgr_pkg.sv lines 264-271.
results.reasoning: This split is the standard keymgr randomness scheme and matches upstream. The two consumers (control-path masking / random key state vs. data-path padding and sw output randomization) intentionally get different mappings to avoid correlation. The assumption only questions whether the asymmetry is deliberate (it is); no contradiction with any guarantee exists. No defect.

results.summary: Replicating data_rand[0] to pad the unused (illegal) stage entries of adv_matrix/id_matrix is acceptable because those entries are only selected for invalid stages, which are independently flagged and never produce a real key.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv line 407 (adv_matrix fill) and line 471 (id_matrix fill) assign {AdvLfsrCopies/IdLfsrCopies{data_rand[0]}} only for the don't-care stage range i in [KeyMgrStages, 2**StageWidth-1]. The legal stages Creator/OwnerInt/Owner get real inputs (lines 439-476). Selecting a fill entry implies an invalid stage, which sets invalid_stage_sel_o (keymgr_ctrl.sv line 285) and is rejected/randomized.
results.reasoning: The padded entries are placeholders for the unused 4th stage encoding (StageWidth=2 gives 4 slots, only 3 are real; keymgr_pkg.sv lines 82, 90-95). data_rand[0] = lfsr[31:0] is a live 32-bit LFSR value, replicated across the wide field. Since these entries are never the basis of a legitimate derived key (invalid stage selection is detected and the operation produces random/garbage output), the entropy quality of the fill is not security-relevant. Matches upstream. No defect.

results.summary: Clearing init_q on en_i deassertion in keymgr_cfg_en is the intended lifecycle-disable behavior; downstream consumers are designed around it.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_cfg_en.sv lines 40-48 clear init_q when (init_q && !en_i). vld_dis = init_q && !en_i (line 32) then forces out_q low (lines 54-55), disabling configuration. This is the intended response to losing the keymgr enable (lifecycle disable). The main FSM independently transitions to StCtrlWipe/StCtrlDisabled when en_i drops (keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 557, 570, 590, 610, 630, 671).
results.reasoning: init_q in keymgr_cfg_en tracks whether the block has been initialized and is intentionally reset by en_i deassertion so that disabling the keymgr re-locks configuration. The downstream consumer (out_o / regwen at keymgr.sv lines 339-372) is built to lock when init_q/en_i drops. The assumption asks to verify downstream consistency; the design is self-consistent. No defect.

results.summary: init_q holding at 1 while en_i stays high is the intended 'has been initialized' latch behavior, not a stuck-enable bug.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_cfg_en.sv lines 40-48: init_q is set when (init_i && en_i) and only cleared by reset or (init_q && !en_i). Remaining at 1 while en_i is high is the deliberate design: init_q records that initialization has occurred and persists until the enable is dropped (or reset). The channel-B SVA '(init_q && en_i) |=> init_q until !en_i' actually describes exactly this correct behavior.
results.reasoning: There is no 'stuck enable' hazard: init_q is a latched status, not a runtime gate that needs to pulse. en_i is driven by the lifecycle controller (keymgr.sv lines 343, 366 via lc_keymgr_en); when lifecycle disables the keymgr, en_i drops and init_q clears. Holding init_q across normal operation is required so configuration locks stay coherent. No defect.
results.formal_alignment: INCONCLUSIVE/SUPPORTIVE. The property (status NAME_UNVERIFIED due to 'until') encodes the correct behavior; no counterexample to intended design.

results.summary: Forcing update_en=0 only in StCtrlWipe controls the latching of last_working_st for software visibility; it is not meant to block key updates, so the 'single point' concern is misdirected.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 703-737: update_en defaults to 1 and is set to 0 only in StCtrlWipe (line 727), where working_state_o is held at last_working_st (line 728). update_en gates the last_working_st flop (lines 695-701), i.e. it preserves the pre-wipe working state for software readback during wipe. Blocking of key updates during wipe is handled separately by the update_sel/KeyUpdateWipe path (lines 230-232, 407-414) and op_req gating, not by update_en.
results.reasoning: The finding assumes update_en is the mechanism that prevents unintended key updates during wipe; in fact update_en only freezes the software-visible working_state register. Actual update suppression in wipe comes from wipe_req forcing KeyUpdateWipe (highest precedence, line 230) which randomizes/wipes key_state, and from the FSM not issuing op_req unless op_busy (line 645). The design is coherent. No defect.

results.summary: The one-cycle-behind working-state reporting and op_done_i gating of status/errors are documented, intended timing; status_o is correctly captured into the register while the operation is in progress.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 739-749 compute status_o (OpIdle/OpWip/OpDoneSuccess/OpDoneFail) from op_done_o and the error/fault vectors. The comment (lines 742-744) explicitly documents the case where an operation finishes the same cycle en_i drops: the main FSM is one cycle behind but still reports fail. error_o[ErrInvalidIn]/[ErrInvalidOp] are gated by op_done_i in keymgr_err.sv lines 132-133 (intended: errors reported at completion).
results.reasoning: status_o is latched into hw2reg.op_status with de=op_start (keymgr.sv lines 302, 331), so the result is captured while op_start is asserted and remains readable. The op_done_i gating in keymgr_err ensures sync errors/faults are surfaced at the operation boundary. The assumption raises a potential misalignment but the documented design handles the en_i-drop corner case. No contradiction found in RTL. No defect.

results.summary: op_done_o being a single-cycle pulse is intended; the status/error result is latched into the op_status register so software does not miss it.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_ctrl.sv line 448 (op_done_o = op_req ? op_ack : init_o | invalid_op) and lines 739-749 (status_o). Although status_o transiently shows OpDoneSuccess/Fail, it is committed to hw2reg.op_status with de=op_start (keymgr.sv lines 302, 331) and start is cleared by op_done (hw2reg.start.de=op_done, line 329). Thus the done/fail status is captured into the register and an interrupt (intr_op_done) is raised (keymgr.sv lines 659-670). Software reads the latched status, not the live pulse.
results.reasoning: The op_done pulse drives both the op_status register capture and the op_done interrupt, so a late-sampling consumer still observes the result via the register/interrupt. This is the standard keymgr completion protocol. The error gating in keymgr_err (op_done_i, lines 132-150) aligns error_o/fault_o with the same completion event. No defect.

results.summary: vld_state_change_q is inherently a single-cycle strobe because vld_state_change_d is only high on the transition cycle (state_d != state_q into a key state); it cannot cause repeated triggers.
results.root_cause: FALSE_ALARM. /home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_ctrl.sv lines 814-833: vld_state_change_d = (state_d != state_q) & (state_d inside {StCtrlRootKey, StCtrlCreatorRootKey, StCtrlOwnerIntKey, StCtrlOwnerKey}). This is true only on the single cycle when the FSM is about to enter one of those key states. Once the transition completes (state_q == state_d on the next edge), the (state_d != state_q) term is false, so vld_state_change_q is high for exactly one cycle. state_change_err = vld_state_change_q & !adv_op (line 833) is therefore evaluated once per transition.
results.reasoning: Entries into the four key states occur via adv_state, which requires op_ack and is not back-to-back; after entering a key state, state_d equals state_q (or moves to a non-key state such as StCtrlInit), driving vld_state_change_d low. Hence vld_state_change_q is a one-cycle pulse and the downstream cross-check (AsyncFaultFsmChk via state_change_err, keymgr_err.sv line 125) fires at most once per state change. The 'held for a full cycle => multiple triggers' assumption is incorrect: one cycle is the intended strobe width and one downstream evaluation results. No defect.
results.formal_alignment: MISLEADING. formal FAIL on 'vld_state_change_q |=> !vld_state_change_q' is a spurious standalone-bind result; in the full design state_d returns to equal state_q after the transition, so the strobe is single-cycle as intended.
